title: OpenAI Responses field-variance prober & adaptive translation suggester
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a diagnostic probe and a runtime 'translation suggester' that discovers field-level variance between Redwood's Responses-compatible surface and actual OpenAI Responses outputs. The probe will generate adversarial/edge-case streams and functioncall event sequences to catalog: 1) field name/key differences, 2) ordering/splitting across stream deltas, 3) structured-output schema drift, and 4) lossiness introduced by tooling (e.g., truncated function args or fragmented JSON). The translation suggester will propose deterministic mapping rules plus a confidence score for runtime application and suggest non-lossy fallback policies.
background: We continue to observe customer-reported regressions and internal test failures when migrating workloads that expect OpenAI Responses semantics. Existing tickets catalog many compatibility gaps, but we lack a focused harness that: a) exercises combinatorial streaming boundaries and functioncall permutations, b) quantifies per-field fidelity loss, and c) proposes safe translation rules. This work aims to bridge that gap with automated probing, a scoring model for 'lossiness', and a runtime component that can propose and optionally apply heuristics in canary deployments.
proposed_solution: Deliver three artifacts: 1) A prober harness (python + ts test runner) that synthesizes streaming/chunking scenarios, mixed tool/functioncall sequences, and malformed-but-plausible structured outputs. The harness will produce normalized deltas and compute a per-field fidelity score (0.0-1.0) and a lossiness taxonomy. 2) A translation suggester service that ingests prober telemetry and proposes transformations (rename, merge, split, reassemble tokens across stream boundaries) with an explainable confidence string and reversible patch instructions. 3) A lightweight runtime proxy that can apply high-confidence translations in Dedicated/Hosted mode with audit logging and a safe rollback mechanism. Telemetry hooks will feed Console dashboards for triage and metric-driven rollouts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Prober generates a corpus of >10k unique stream/funccall permutations and outputs a catalog in CSV/JSON (schema: field, observed_variants, fidelity_score, examples)
- Translation suggester produces deterministic mapping proposals for at least 90% of cataloged variants with confidence metadata
- Runtime proxy can apply mappings in a canary for a single customer without functional regressions (canary run documented)
- Unit + integration tests covering key edge cases (split JSON across two stream chunks, interleaved function calls, simultaneous name collisions)
- Dashboards in Console showing fidelity-by-model, fidelity-by-route, and top-5 failing mappings
- Design and runbook for manual fallback and customer communication prepared and reviewed
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for parser and reassembly logic (split-chunk rejoin, token boundary heuristics)
2) Fuzz tests: randomize field ordering, nested arrays, partial tool metadata; validate translation suggester outputs are idempotent
3) Integration: deploy prober against internal staging of Redwood-hosted OpenAI Responses shim and also against a pinned OpenAI endpoint; compare deltas
4) Load test runtime proxy at targeted QPS (100r/s) to measure added latency and error rates
5) Canary: rollout mapping for a non-critical customer, collect metrics for 7 days, evaluate quality delta and error budget impact
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1: Internal validation (prober + suggester) on staging (2 weeks)
- Phase 2: Canary runtime proxy for internal Redwood tenant (3 days)
- Phase 3: Partner canary with 1-2 low-risk customers, feature flag enabled, 7-day observation
- Phase 4: Gradual ramp to broader customers with automated rollback rules (fidelity drop > 5% or error rate > 0.5%)
progress_updates:
2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with PM (Lena Ortiz) and Design (Omar Ruiz). Agreed scope to start with streaming/fncall permutations and defer structured-output schema inference to follow-up.
2025-02-18: Prototype prober: basic stream splitter + functioncall interleaver implemented. Early runs show frequent 'arg-key' fragmentation when chunk size < 64 bytes.
2025-02-26: Translation suggester v0: simple heuristics (key normalization, common alias map) generated 64% coverage on staging corpus. Decided to add n-gram and structural context scoring.
2025-03-01: Security review intake created; design doc posted. Marcus implemented audit logging prototype for proxy.
2025-03-04: PM feedback: ensure canary path includes customer comms template and rollback SLA. Added to rollout plan. Current blockers: perf baseline for proxy (measuring overhead) and test corpus growth speed.
